summary: The residential half of Block D at 3rd and Mission Rock streets: a Residential Mixed Use tower entitled to 240 ft (one of three 240-ft sites with Blocks A and F) wrapping the Block D2 parking structure along Third Street, with roughly 250,000 gsf of housing in the EIR description. Not yet built as far as the record shows: the Port's June 5, 2026 staff memo says Phase 1 was completed in 2025 and Phase 2 is in pre-development, and the Commission's June 9, 2026 minutes record its $10 million Phase 2 pre-development item (Resolution 26-34) as passed unanimously (neither document names Block D1).

milestones.text: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA and Design Controls that set this block's use and envelope (among Resolutions 18-03 to 18-10, which the Jan 30, 2018 minutes record as adopted)

Board of Supervisors affirms the EIR certification and approvals (File No. 171286 per the Notice of Determination; the Port's Oct 2023 report calls No. 33-18 a Resolution and its June 2026 report an Ordinance); Notice of Determination filed March 9, 2018

Development Agreement takes effect (the Port's fact sheet gives its effective date as Aug. 15, 2018; SF Planning's project page dates both the Development Agreement and the Disposition and Development Agreement 8/15/2018); DA term 30 years, four phases

Draft EIR describes Block D as two attached buildings totaling about 1.1 million gsf, with roughly 250,000 gsf of residential along Third Street; illustrative phasing put Block D in Area 2 (2018-2021)

Developer sends the Port its Phase 2 Submittal (with a Garage Report submitted October 14, 2022 and a Basis of Design November 18, 2022); the budget and appraisal elements are deferred. The Port's memo says 'Phase 2 will include the parking garage' and does not say which blocks the Submittal covers, so its link to Block D1 is not established

Port Commission adopts Resolution 23-46 (passed unanimously as amended, with non-substantive changes); its recitals state that Phase 2 is 'not currently financially feasible' and that Port and Developer staff 'mutually agreed earlier this year to decelerate work on Phase 2 while waiting for macroeconomic conditions to improve'

Port staff say later phases 'may require higher percentages of BMR units' to reach the project's 40% target after Phase 1 was cut to 132 BMR units; the Port, developer and MOHCD are reviewing changes 'with the goal of improving the feasibility of future Phases of Mission Rock and accelerating development' (Resolution 25-17)

Port Commission approves Resolution 26-34, authorizing up to $10 million in Port Capital as pre-development funding for Phase 2 (for eligible Phase 2 pre-development costs, including 'design and engineering for Phase 2 infrastructure; Developer, Port, and City staff costs; consultant expenses'; the memo separately says the Developer will advance pre-development and design work for the vertical buildings in parallel), intended to avoid a 12-18 month delay to construction readiness. Staff's schedule lists a 'Potential Construction Start' of Summer/Fall 2027 for horizontal infrastructure and vertical building construction, and the memo says Phase 2 could begin construction 'as early as 2027' once anchor tenants are secured; its Table 1 gives illustrative repayment scenarios for a 2027, 2028 or 2029 vertical start -- not a committed date for this or any other Phase 2 block.

Third Street and Mission Rock Street; the residential building wraps the garage along Third Street
Port of San Francisco (Seawall Lot 337); future parcel to be ground-leased for 75 years under the DDA

Phase 2 submittal delivered December 2022; decelerated in 2023 as infeasible; Port's October 2023 repayment model assumed a hypothetical March 2026 Phase 2 start

details.text: Height of Block D1: on Design Controls p.191, the '80.00' and '305.00' MINIMUM labels are horizontal dimensions along the base, not heights.

open_questions: The Design Controls' Section 6.5.2 (Design Intent: Block D1) does say 'Block D1 marks the Mission Rock MUNI Metro Station'; located in the April 2018 text 2026-09-29.

Unit count and affordability for D1: none set; the Port's March 2025 memo says the 2025 Phase 1 changes 'will require that later phases of the Project may require higher percentages of BMR units to meet the 40% overall target' (no per-phase figure is given).

No construction start, Phase 2 budget approval or vertical design submittal for this block was found; the Port's June 5, 2026 staff memo schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal for Winter/Spring 2027. No source read states Block D1's present condition, so whether it remains part of the Seawall Lot 337 parking lot (Lot A) is not confirmed.
Which blocks the December 2022 Phase 2 Submittal covers is not stated in the Port memos read; only the Phase 2 parking garage is named.
The DDA 'Outside Dates' for commencing later phases are in the DDA itself, which was not read.
No cost, developer capital or land-value figure exists for this block; the Port says Phase 2 appraisals are deferred until the market supports the minimum land values.

Images: no rendering specific to this block exists in the public-record documents read (the Design Controls give only diagrammatic envelopes), and the 2026 aerial serves as the 'before'/'now' view of the parking lot it sits in.

No expected-completion date could be sourced for Block D1. The Mission Rock Design Controls (208 pages, checked in full) contain no phasing schedule at all. The Disposition and Development Agreement (DDA; Board of Supervisors File No. 180092, adopted as Resolution 42-18 on 2/13/2018) was not read for this record, so which phase includes Parcel D1 and any DDA schedule dates are not confirmed here; the Draft EIR's illustrative phasing put Block D in Area 2, and the Port's October 2023 memo says Phase 2 will include the parking garage. The Port's fact sheet gives 8/15/2018 as the Development Agreement's effective date, and no source read states the DDA's own effective date. Phase 2 was found 'not currently financially feasible' in October 2023 (see this record's milestones), and the Port's June 2026 memo gives only a potential construction start, with no block-specific date (see the next question), so no basis (record, phase or project) supports an expected-completion date for this block.

As of 2026-09-21: the June 9, 2026 Port Commission item (Resolution 26-34, $10M pre-development investment) updates the earlier finding above that no Port memo gives a revised target year -- Port staff now have a schedule for Phase 2 pre-development work (contractor procurement 'Winter - Summer 2027') and a 'Potential Construction Start' of Summer/Fall 2027; the memo says construction could begin 'as early as 2027' once anchor tenants are secured and gives 2027/2028/2029 vertical-start scenarios only as illustrative repayment estimates, not a single committed date -- still no basis (record, phase or project) for an expected-completion milestone for this block specifically.

Area of Block D1: the 97,498 sq ft (2.24 acres) figure is for Block D as a whole in the developer's March 2012 proposal, which predates the 2018 Design Controls that divide the block into D1 and D2; the table gives no D1/D2 split and the block outline may have changed.

Driveways for Block D1: the Design Controls provide driveways at the shared Block D parking facility ('Driveways shall be provided at Block D to accommodate parking facility ingress and egress'); no separate D1 driveway is stated in the passages found.
